missing_details: The polynomial must have degree n ≥ 2
All roots lie in the closed unit disk { z∈ℂ : |z| ≤ 1 }
Critical points are defined as the zeros of the derivative f′
Each root must be within distance 1 of at least one critical point
The statement is over the field of complex numbers
refined_question: Let f(z) be a complex polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with factorization f(z)=(z−r₁)(z−r₂)…(z−rₙ), where each zero rᵢ satisfies |rᵢ| ≤ 1. Denote by f′ the derivative of f and by c₁,…,c_{n−1} its zeros (the critical points of f). Is it true that for every i∈{1,…,n} there exists j∈{1,…,n−1} such that |c_{j}−r_{i}| ≤ 1?
justification: The canonical statement is taken verbatim from the Wikipedia article 'Sendov's conjecture,' which specifies all necessary conditions (degree constraint, domain of roots, definition of critical points, and the distance bound) and remains the standard open problem in complex analysis ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture)). The conjecture’s name alone omits these quantitative details and precise definitions, which have been restored in the refined, self-contained question.
